proposed.choice: Package a thin Node CLI adapter, one Rust browser engine, the static HTML/CSS/JavaScript reader and bundled D2.
proposed.rationale: Retain the public CLI while giving one engine ownership of capture, projection and native publication/recovery. Native locking and no-replace rename support the existing filesystem contract; no performance claim is assumed.
alternatives: Node-only engine with an additional native filesystem dependency or another qualified publication protocol.
Node generator with a separate native publisher.
Node wrapper around the current Python generator.
consequences: Adds a pinned Rust build, Cargo lockfile, platform executable and bounded browser-engine-v1 subprocess protocol; customers need no Rust compiler.
Current Python scripts remain the observed prototype until coordinated replacement; no permanent dual semantic engines are intended.
Use D2 0.9.0 for both generated projections and registered authored design diagrams; keep one authoritative source for each diagram and use plain-language conditions.
Package completeness and clean-customer qualification precede public support.

The owning technical model maps components and contracts to existing Modules. Logical presents that technical structure; Development presents intended source units, packages and build resources from the same design.
revisit_when: A selected requirement, supported platform or actual qualification result defeats this realization.
